newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil council would let Korea Exchange operate.
newsitem.headline: Brazil council would let Korea Exchange operate.

text.p: Brazil's National Monetary Council (CMN) has asked President Fernando Henrique Cardoso to allow the Korea Exchange Bank to operate in Brazil, said Central Bank Director of Controls Alkimar Moura.

Moura said the South Korean government had agreed to allow Brazilian banks to set up operations there in return if Korea Exchange were authorized in Brazil, adding Brasilia projected Korean investment in Brazil would reach $5.0 billion by the year 2000.
Moura told reporters Korea Exchange planned to set up as a multiple bank.

He said Korea Exchange officials had indicated the bank would set up $100-150 million in credit lines for Brazilian banks, $300 million for commercial loans and $500 million in credit for Korean firms operating in Brazil.
"This will increase competition in the Brazilian financial system," Moura told reporters after a regular CMN meeting.
President Cardoso must still sign a decree allowing Korea Exchange to set up.
